name: load_csv
description: Loads a CSV file into memory as a pandas DataFrame. Call this before any other tool. Returns the dataset shape, column names, and a preview of the first five rows.

returns.description: Dataset shape, column names, and first five rows.

name: analyze_data
description: Performs exploratory data analysis on the loaded dataset. Returns descriptive statistics, missing value counts, duplicate row count, unique value counts per column, data types, and the correlation matrix for numeric columns.

returns.description: Full EDA report including stats, nulls, duplicates, and correlations.

name: run_pandas_code
description: Executes custom Python/pandas code on the loaded DataFrame. The DataFrame is available as 'df'. Use this for any custom analysis, filtering, grouping, aggregation, sorting, or transformation. Any resulting DataFrame will be captured and rendered as an interactive table.

code.description: Python pandas code to execute. Use 'df' to access the dataset. Use print() for output or assign/evaluate a filtered DataFrame.

returns.description: Printed output or tabular preview from the code, or an error message.

name: run_sql_query
description: Executes a SQL query on the loaded dataset using DuckDB. The dataset table name in SQL is 'df'. Use this for analytical queries, aggregations, filtering, group by, window functions, and retrieving rows. When the user asks for records or filtered rows (e.g. 'give me all male customers...'), execute 'SELECT * FROM df WHERE ...' to retrieve the actual records.

query.description: SQL query to execute against the 'df' table. Example: 'SELECT column1, COUNT(*) FROM df GROUP BY column1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10'

returns.description: Tabular results of the SQL query or an error message.

name: plot_chart
description: Generates a chart from the loaded dataset and saves it as an image. Supported types: bar, line, scatter, hist, pie.

y.description: Column name for the y-axis. Not required for histograms.

returns.description: File path of the saved chart image.

name: remove_duplicates
description: Removes rows that are exact duplicates across every column, keeping the first occurrence. Does not accept any parameters - always performs full-row comparison.

returns.description: Number of duplicate rows removed and rows remaining.

name: handle_missing_values
description: Automatically imputes or cleans missing (null/NaN) values in the loaded dataset using various statistical strategies and returns a detailed before/after summary. Changes are saved directly to the active dataset.

strategy.description: Imputation or cleaning strategy: 'mean' (numeric only), 'median' (numeric only), 'mode' (most frequent value), 'drop' (remove rows with missing values), or 'fill' (fill with specified fill_value).

columns.description: Optional list of column names to apply the strategy to. If omitted, applies to all columns with missing values (or all numeric columns for mean/median).

fill_value.description: The constant value to use when strategy is 'fill'. Can be a string, number, or boolean.

returns.description: A detailed before/after summary report of missing values and dataset shape.

name: detect_and_handle_outliers
description: Detects statistical outliers in numeric columns using IQR (Interquartile Range) or Z-score method and handles them via clipping (winsorizing), dropping rows, or creating flag columns. Prevents skewed distributions without breaking the dataset.

columns.description: Optional list of numeric column names to analyze. If omitted, analyzes all numeric columns in the dataset.

method.description: Outlier detection method: 'iqr' (1.5 * IQR rule) or 'zscore' (standard score threshold |z| > 3). Defaults to 'iqr'.

action.description: Action to take on detected outliers: 'clip' (cap outliers at lower/upper bounds), 'drop' (remove rows containing outliers), or 'flag' (add boolean column '{column}_outlier' marking outliers). Defaults to 'clip'.

returns.description: A summary report of detected outliers per column, bounds calculated, action applied, and dataset shape.

name: convert_column_types
description: Parses messy dates, strips currency symbols ($, €, £, ¥, ₹) and formatting commas, and cleanly converts column data types in the active dataset. Returns a summary of converted columns.

column_mapping.description: Dictionary mapping column names to target data types. Supported types: 'numeric' / 'float', 'integer' / 'int', 'datetime' / 'date', 'string' / 'str', 'boolean' / 'bool', 'categorical'. Example: {"order_date": "datetime", "price": "numeric"}

returns.description: A summary report of converted columns, old and new data types, and any coerced values.

name: export_csv
description: Exports the current dataset to a CSV file and returns the file path. Call this when the user wants to download or save the dataset after cleaning or analysis. The filename parameter is optional - if not specified, the file will be named 'exported_dataset.csv'.

filename.description: Optional name for the output file (without or with .csv extension). Defaults to 'exported_dataset'.

returns.description: File path of the saved CSV file.
